name: Fuzzy Miner
author: Promenade Team
description: Günther & van der Aalst's Fuzzy Miner for case-centric event logs: instead of a control-flow model it measures the log from several perspectives — frequency and routing significance per activity, frequency and distance significance per relation, and proximity, endpoint and originator correlation — and hands back the whole weighted graph. Simplification is interactive: the Fuzzy graph view's collapsible slider rail resolves concurrency conflicts, thins edges and folds insignificant activities into clusters, live, exactly the way ProM's original does.

maximalDistance.title: Maximal event distance
maximalDistance.description: How many events back a relation is still counted. 1 is the plain directly-follows relation; the original's default of 5 also credits indirect successors, attenuated by how far away they are. ProM's own GUI allows up to 100; this caps at 20 to keep the scan's memory bounded at the activity limit's upper end — comfortably past anything the reference implementation's own default (5) or its batch operator's own default (1) ever exercises.

attenuation.title: Attenuation
attenuation.description: How fast a relation's weight decays with distance. "Nth root" divides by the radical once per step (the original's default); "Linear" fades evenly across the radical's worth of steps and then to nothing.

radical.title: Radical
radical.description: The attenuation's steepness — ProM calls it the radical, or the number of echelons. Larger means a faster decay under "Nth root", a longer reach under "Linear".

frequencySignificanceUnary.title: Weight: frequency significance (activity)
frequencySignificanceUnary.description: How much an activity's raw occurrence count contributes to its significance. 0 excludes the metric entirely.

invertFrequencySignificanceUnary.title: Invert: frequency significance (activity)
invertFrequencySignificanceUnary.description: Flip this metric so the least frequent activities score highest instead of the most frequent ones.

routingSignificanceUnary.title: Weight: routing significance (activity)
routingSignificanceUnary.description: How much an activity's in/out imbalance contributes to its significance. A pure split or join scores 1, a pass-through 0 — it is what keeps a rare but structurally decisive activity on the map.

invertRoutingSignificanceUnary.title: Invert: routing significance (activity)
invertRoutingSignificanceUnary.description: Flip this metric so a pass-through activity scores highest instead of a pure split or join.

frequencySignificanceBinary.title: Weight: frequency significance (relation)
frequencySignificanceBinary.description: How much a relation's attenuated observation count contributes to its significance.

invertFrequencySignificanceBinary.title: Invert: frequency significance (relation)
invertFrequencySignificanceBinary.description: Flip this metric so the least-observed relations score highest instead of the most-observed ones.

distanceSignificanceBinary.title: Weight: distance significance (relation)
distanceSignificanceBinary.description: Penalises a weak relation between two highly significant activities — the signature of a long-distance shortcut rather than a real hand-off.

invertDistanceSignificanceBinary.title: Invert: distance significance (relation)
invertDistanceSignificanceBinary.description: Flip this metric so a long-distance shortcut between two significant activities scores highest instead of lowest.

proximityCorrelation.title: Weight: proximity correlation
proximityCorrelation.description: Two events close together in time are more likely to belong together. Needs timestamps.

invertProximityCorrelation.title: Invert: proximity correlation
invertProximityCorrelation.description: Flip this metric so events far apart in time score highest instead of events close together.

endpointCorrelation.title: Weight: endpoint correlation
endpointCorrelation.description: How similar the two activity names are, by edit distance — "Check invoice" and "Check order" look related, and in most logs that naming is not an accident.

invertEndpointCorrelation.title: Invert: endpoint correlation
invertEndpointCorrelation.description: Flip this metric so dissimilarly named activities score highest instead of similarly named ones.

originatorCorrelation.title: Weight: originator correlation
originatorCorrelation.description: How similar the two events' org:resource values are. Silently contributes nothing on a log without resources — the Statistics panel reports whether this log has any.

invertOriginatorCorrelation.title: Invert: originator correlation
invertOriginatorCorrelation.description: Flip this metric so events done by different resources score highest instead of events done by the same resource.

includeMetricDetail.title: Keep per-metric values
includeMetricDetail.description: Carry each metric's own normalised matrix in the result, not just the weighted totals. Roughly quadruples the model's size; off unless you want to inspect the individual perspectives.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Keeps only the most frequent activities. The metrics are n×n matrices, so this is the one setting that changes what has to be re-scanned.

nodeCutoff.title: Node cutoff
nodeCutoff.description: Activities below this significance are folded into clusters, or dropped when clustering cannot place them.

edgeTransform.title: Edge transformer
edgeTransform.description: "Fuzzy edges" keeps, per activity, every relation within the cutoff of its best one. "Best edges" keeps only the single strongest predecessor and successor.

edgeCutoff.title: Edge cutoff
edgeCutoff.description: How far below an activity's strongest relation a relation may fall and still be drawn. 0 keeps only the best, 1 keeps everything.

utilityRatio.title: Utility ratio
utilityRatio.description: How the edge filter ranks a relation: 1 purely by significance, 0 purely by correlation.

interpretAbsolute.title: Interpret cutoff absolutely
interpretAbsolute.description: Rank an activity's incoming and outgoing relations against one shared range instead of two separate ones.

ignoreSelfLoops.title: Ignore self-loops
ignoreSelfLoops.description: Leave self-loops out of the edge filter's ranking, so a dominant self-loop cannot suppress an activity's real relations.

filterConcurrency.title: Resolve concurrency
filterConcurrency.description: Where A and B relate in both directions, decide whether that is genuine concurrency or an artifact, and drop the artifact.

concurrencyPreserve.title: Preserve threshold
concurrencyPreserve.description: A two-way relation whose halves are both this important to their endpoints is left alone as real concurrency.

concurrencyRatio.title: Ratio threshold
concurrencyRatio.description: How lopsided the two halves must be before the weaker one is treated as noise and removed on its own. Above this, both go.

edgeLabel.title: Edge labels
edgeLabel.description: What to print on each arc.

dropDisconnected.title: Hide disconnected activities
dropDisconnected.description: Leave out an activity that survived every filter but ended up with no relations at all.

mode.title: View
mode.description: Matrix shows the binary (per-pair) metrics as a coloured grid; Curves shows the unary (per-activity) metrics overlaid as line charts, ProM's other Fuzzy Miner metrics panel; Distances is a diagnostic ProM doesn't have: how many relation observations the scan found at each look-back distance, with the current attenuation curve overlaid, to inform whether raising the maximal distance (set on the action itself) would actually capture more.

metric.title: Matrix metric
metric.description: Which binary metric colours the grid. The two weighted totals are always available; the five raw metrics behind them need the model to have been mined with "Keep per-metric values" enabled.

rowMetric.title: Row metric
rowMetric.description: The unary (per-activity) metric shown as a bar in the row gutter, next to each activity's name.

sort.title: Sort activities
sort.description: The order activities appear in on both axes.

cellSize.title: Cell size
cellSize.description: Pixel size of one matrix cell.

citation.text: Günther, C.W., van der Aalst, W.M.P. (2007). Fuzzy Mining – Adaptive Process Simplification Based on Multi-Perspective Metrics. In: Business Process Management (BPM 2007), LNCS 4714, pp. 328–343.
